meta.title: Get palaia running
meta.description: The simplest way is to let an AI assistant set it up for you. Cloud-server, NAS, Docker and Compose options are here too.

lede: palaia lives on an always-on box that your AI tools reach from anywhere — a small cloud server, a NAS, a spare mini-PC. The simplest way to set it up is to let an AI assistant do it for you; every do-it-yourself path is below.

ai.h2: Let your AI set it up
ai.intro: You do not have to touch a terminal. Copy the prompt below, paste it into an AI assistant you already use, and it reads the setup guide and walks you through it — one step at a time, in plain language.
ai.promptLabel: Paste this into your AI assistant
ai.prompt: Set palaia up for me. First read get.palaia.ai/skill, then walk me through it step by step — I'm not technical, so explain everything simply.
ai.hint: The assistant asks where palaia should run and does the rest.

manual.intro: All of these end at the same hub. The cloud-server path needs no terminal; the rest are for people comfortable with a command line or Docker.

cloud.h2: A cloud server in three steps
cloud.fine: No terminal, no SSH. You paste one file when you create the server and it sets itself up. Any small provider works — Hetzner Cloud and DigitalOcean are good, inexpensive picks; the smallest size is plenty.
cloud.step1Body: Sign in to your provider and begin creating a new server (a "Cloud Server" or "Droplet"). Pick any recent Ubuntu or Debian image and the smallest size — leave the page open at the step where it offers a Cloud config or User data field. That field is where the file in step 3 goes.
cloud.step2Body: palaia joins a tailnet — a small private network of just your own devices (via Tailscale, free for personal use), so your hub is reachable from your phone and laptop but never from the open internet. Create a free Tailscale account, then open the auth-keys page and generate one key (a reusable, ephemeral key works well). Copy it — you paste it into the file in the next step.
cloud.step3H3: Paste this file, replace the key, create the server
cloud.step3Body: Copy the file below into the provider's Cloud config / User data field. Change the one line it marks — TAILSCALE_AUTH_KEY="tskey-REPLACE_ME" near the top — to the key from step 2. Nothing else needs editing. Then create the server.
cloud.afterNote: A couple of minutes after the server boots it installs everything and starts the hub by itself. Then open your hub at its tailnet address. If it does not come up, the server's /var/log/cloud-init-output.log has the full log of what ran.

existing.h2: Already have a server? One command over SSH
existing.body: The file above only runs on a server's first boot, so pasting it into a box that is already running does nothing. owned.h2: Or a machine you already own
owned.fine: The developer options below install the same hub on any of these:
owned.machineRaspberry: Raspberry Pi or another small always-on box — works today with 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS and Docker installed, then the Docker command below. A flash-and-boot card image that skips even those steps is planned and tracked in the open.
owned.machineSynology: Synology NAS — its Container Manager runs a Compose file as a "project"; no terminal on the NAS itself. See the step-by-step Synology walkthrough.
owned.machineDesktop: Mac or Windows — install Docker Desktop once, then the Docker command below is the whole install. (Best for trying palaia out — for everyday use a box that stays on wins.)

dev.fine: Already run containers? Install the hub straight from the image.
dev.rcNote: Release candidate. The commands here still name the :stable image, which is not published until 3.0.0 is final. Until then use :beta instead — e.g. ghcr.io/byte5ai/palaia-hub:beta. The cloud-server file and the get.palaia.ai one-liner above already target :beta, so there is nothing to change there.

dev.curlFine: Want a script that installs Docker and Tailscale for you and prints the address at the end? That is the one command over SSH above — curl … get.palaia.ai | sh.
dev.composeBody: Prefer a config file you can edit and check in, or already run other containers this way? Clone the repository and start it with Compose:
dev.composeFine: A ready-to-use docker-compose.yml ships in that repository at v3/deploy/ — nothing to write yourself.
dev.storesBody: Packages for these platforms are built and kept current in the repository, but none is listed in an official app catalog yet — a submission step still to happen, tracked in the open. Until a listing goes live, Docker or Compose above install the same image on any of them, since they all run containers underneath.

open.body: On a cloud or SSH setup, open http://<your-tailnet-address>:8420/ from any device on your tailnet (the setup prints the address when it finishes). On a machine on your own network, open http://palaia.local — or, if that address does not resolve yet (some setups need one network flag; see Install it for the one-line fix), the http://<host>:8420 address printed to the container's own log, which always works.

wizard.body: From there a short setup wizard runs in the browser: an administrator sign-in, your first memory, and connecting the first AI tool you use — no file editing, no extra commands. See Your first shared memory for what that looks like end to end, or Install it for the longer version of everything on this page.
